title: How a Man of God Handles the Urge Before It Becomes a Habit
caption:
The habit doesn't start where you think it does.

It starts as a hand reaching for your phone before you've thought a single word. The scroll, the second look, the reply you shouldn't send. By the time you're calling it a habit, you've already lost the first ten seconds a dozen times.

A man of God doesn't win that fight at the habit. He wins it at the urge, before it has a name. He asks what it's actually standing in for. He decides in the morning what he won't do at night, so the fight is smaller before it starts. And when he loses a round, he says it out loud to one brother that same week.

"Submit to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you." (James 4:7)

The urge doesn't run your life. You run it, and He runs you.

theme: He runs his life — his impulses don't control him.
